title: Quality of Earnings
summary: Quality of Earnings explains whether reported EBITDA is durable, repeatable, and believable enough to underwrite or sell.
definition: Quality of Earnings is the diligence process used to validate normalized EBITDA, revenue quality, margin sustainability, working capital behavior, and financial reporting integrity.
whyItMatters: PE operators care because every dollar of credible EBITDA can be multiplied at exit, while weak add-backs and poor revenue quality destroy valuation trust.
example: A buyer may reject a seller's adjusted EBITDA if customer churn, one-time projects, or aggressive add-backs prove earnings are less repeatable than presented.

articleSections.title: Use Quality of Earnings to Establish an Underwritable Baseline
body: A quality of earnings review establishes how much historical earnings are recurring, correctly measured, and transferable to a new owner. It is not an audit opinion, a valuation, or a guarantee of future performance. The work begins with reported financial statements and the general ledger, then reconciles revenue, cost, and balance-sheet behavior to normalized EBITDA and cash conversion. Buyers use the result to set the earnings base for price and leverage; sellers use it to identify challenges before the market does. The central question is whether a knowledgeable owner can reproduce the earnings without relying on unusual timing, unsupported estimates, or costs deferred into the future.

Evidence should form a traceable chain. Audited statements tie to trial balances; trial balances tie to monthly general-ledger detail; revenue ties to invoices, contracts, cash receipts, and operational data; payroll ties to employee records; and proposed adjustments tie to invoices, agreements, or named events. Interviews explain anomalies but do not replace records. A conclusion should state the period, accounting policy, sample or population tested, limitation, and sensitivity. If source data cannot distinguish recurring services from one-time projects, the reviewer should quantify the uncertainty rather than convert management confidence into adjusted EBITDA.

Governance protects independence and speed. The sponsor's deal lead owns the underwriting decision, the QoE provider owns its analysis, management owns complete and accurate data, the CFO coordinates responses, and commercial and operating teams validate customer and process explanations. A weekly issues meeting should move to twice weekly near exclusivity, with an aging request list and explicit owners. The first gate is reconciled source data; the second is a supported adjustment bridge; the final gate is an integrated earnings, working-capital, and debt-capacity view. No open issue should disappear merely because the investment committee date arrives.
articleSections.callout: A QoE conclusion is only as strong as the evidence chain from financial statement to ledger, transaction, contract, cash, and operating reality.

articleSections.title: Construct and Challenge the Adjusted EBITDA Bridge
body: The adjusted EBITDA bridge should start with reported EBITDA for a defined period and classify each adjustment by economic cause. Valid normalizations may correct accounting errors, remove a demonstrably nonrecurring event, replace owner compensation with a market cost, or reflect an executed change already visible in the run rate. The bridge distinguishes historical normalization from forecast synergy. Procurement opportunities, unimplemented headcount reductions, future cross-sell, and hypothetical pricing are value-creation initiatives, not historical earnings. Each line needs a gross amount, offsets, tax or cost consequences where relevant, evidence, responsible executive, and status as accepted, rejected, or sensitivity only.

A worked case makes the discipline visible. Reported trailing-twelve-month EBITDA is $18.0 million. Add $1.2 million for a settled, uninsured litigation matter and $0.8 million to normalize above-market owner compensation. Subtract $0.7 million of revenue recognized before delivery and subtract $0.5 million of recurring temporary labor that management called one-time. Supported adjusted EBITDA is therefore $18.8 million: $18.0 million plus $2.0 million of accepted add-backs less $1.2 million of downward adjustments. A proposed $1.5 million future procurement saving remains outside QoE and belongs in the value-creation case.

The review should attack recurrence, completeness, and double counting. Repeated restructuring charges, annual recruiting projects, chronic overtime, routine legal costs, and recurring freight premiums do not become exceptional because account descriptions change. Lost-customer costs cannot be added back while retaining the customer's historical profit. A vacant role adjustment must include the replacement salary if the role is necessary. Management and the provider should maintain a single adjustment register tied to ledger entries and the model. The acceptance gate is not plausibility; it is evidence that the cost or revenue treatment will not recur under normal ownership.

articleSections.title: Connect Revenue Quality, Margins, and Working Capital
body: Revenue quality asks how revenue is earned, recognized, retained, concentrated, and converted to cash. Analysis should segment recurring subscriptions, usage, projects, products, pass-through items, and acquisitions; then measure cohort retention, contract terms, churn, price, volume, mix, backlog conversion, credits, and cut-off. A high recurring-revenue label is insufficient if contracts are cancellable, implementation capacity constrains activation, or a few customers drive growth. Monthly sales data should reconcile to the ledger, and major variances should reconcile to customers and invoices. Commercial diligence may assess market demand, but QoE establishes whether the historical revenue record is internally consistent and collectible.

Margin durability requires a bridge from revenue to gross profit and operating expense. Reviewers test whether improvement came from price realization, favorable mix, procurement, productivity, capitalization, classification changes, deferred maintenance, or temporary understaffing. If service levels deteriorated while labor cost fell, the apparent margin may require reinvestment. If freight moved below gross profit, comparability is broken even though EBITDA is unchanged. Unit economics, warranty claims, overtime, utilization, headcount vacancies, and capex trends help distinguish structural productivity from earnings borrowed from customers, employees, suppliers, or equipment.

Working capital provides an independent check on the income statement. Revenue that rises while receivable days and credit memos deteriorate may reflect collection risk or aggressive cut-off. Margin gains accompanied by obsolete inventory or unpaid vendors may not convert to cash. The QoE team should reconcile EBITDA to operating cash flow and explain changes in receivables, inventory, payables, deferred revenue, and accrued expenses. A normalized net working capital schedule uses the same policies and segmentation as the earnings analysis. Otherwise, an item excluded from EBITDA can be charged again through the purchase-price adjustment, or a temporary cash benefit can be mistaken for recurring earnings quality.

articleSections.title: Prepare the Business and Challenge the Findings
body: Preparation begins with reliable monthly closes, consistent account mappings, documented revenue-recognition and reserve policies, and reconciled operational KPIs. The CFO should maintain a data dictionary, acquisition and pro forma schedules, customer and SKU bridges, payroll roster, related-party list, nonrecurring-item log, and working-capital history. An internal dry run should reproduce trailing-twelve-month EBITDA from ledger data and identify unsupported adjustments before a sell-side report begins. The goal is not to manufacture add-backs; it is to remove avoidable ambiguity so management can spend diligence time explaining business drivers instead of rebuilding basic records.

A robust challenge process assigns every finding a disposition. Management may accept it, correct the source, produce contrary evidence, or quantify a remaining range. The sponsor should test both the provider's methods and management's narrative: Was the full population examined? Does an adjustment recur in earlier years? Are acquisitions consistently pro formed? Do revenue and receivables tell the same story? Does the conclusion survive a cut-off shift or customer loss? A red-team session before finalization should focus on the five largest valuation and leverage sensitivities, with the investment committee deciding which amount enters base, downside, or upside cases.

Common failure modes are predictable. Data-room dumps obscure missing periods; spreadsheets sever the link to the ledger; management presents net adjustments without adverse offsets; annual results hide monthly volatility; and reviewers accept run-rate savings before implementation. Another failure is scope confusion: QoE cannot replace tax, legal, commercial, cyber, or operational diligence. The completion gate requires reconciled financials, a closed or explicitly qualified request list, a bridge with no duplicate entries, and an issues summary that states what was not tested. Known limitations should lower confidence or change price, structure, leverage, or closing conditions rather than vanish in a footnote.

articleSections.title: Translate Earnings Quality into Debt Capacity, Valuation, and Exit Proof
body: Normalized EBITDA affects both sides of the acquisition capitalization. At a 10.0x multiple, the difference between the seller's $21.5 million claim and the supported $18.8 million case is $27 million of enterprise value. If lenders size debt at 5.0x, the same $2.7 million gap reduces debt capacity by $13.5 million, potentially requiring more sponsor equity while returns fall. The downside case should also stress cash conversion, customer loss, required reinvestment, and covenant definitions because lender EBITDA may exclude adjustments that a purchase-price model accepts. A single optimistic bridge should never drive price, leverage, and liquidity simultaneously.

After close, the QoE bridge becomes an operating baseline rather than a forgotten report. Finance should convert accepted findings into monthly controls: revenue cut-off testing, adjustment-register updates, customer and margin cohorts, reserve governance, EBITDA-to-cash reconciliation, and working-capital reporting. The CFO owns the close; business leaders own operational explanations and corrective actions; the operating partner and board review major deviations quarterly. If the $18.8 million baseline falls short, the bridge should distinguish volume, price, mix, churn, labor, input cost, investment, and accounting effects so the sponsor can respond before covenant or liquidity pressure emerges.

At exit, buyers pay for earnings they can independently reproduce and for growth that does not require hidden reinvestment. A multi-year record of clean closes, consistent definitions, customer retention, margin bridges, cash conversion, and resolved control gaps reduces retrading risk and supports debt financing for the next buyer. Exit readiness should begin twelve to twenty-four months before sale with an internal QoE refresh and monthly evidence pack. The strongest outcome is not the largest adjusted EBITDA number; it is a durable bridge from reported results to normalized earnings that survives buyer diligence, lender review, management questioning, and the passage of time.

diagrams.title: Quality of Earnings Evidence and Decision Flow
diagrams.description: Source evidence supports the EBITDA bridge, which is tested against revenue, margin, working-capital, and cash behavior before entering valuation and leverage cases.
